notes: Plan-mode approval pause on hermes. Hermes' plan mode is the bundled `plan` skill invoked as `/plan` (verified live: scan_skill_commands() returns {'/plan': 'plan'}); it is PROMPT-level — there is no exit_plan_mode tool, no mode enum and no read-only enforcement anywhere in the 0.19.0 source. That is why this cell is observable where the gemini-cli / mistral-vibe / aider / opencode siblings are frozen: their approval gate blocks MID-turn and flushes nothing, while hermes' pause IS the turn boundary. The agent finishes the turn asking for approval, and hermes persists that as an ordinary row in the one shared store ($HERMES_HOME/state.db, observed via agent.ProcessOwnedStore — hermes writes no transcript file): role='assistant', finish_reason='stop', content carrying the ask. parser.go sets PendingWaitingCue from that row's FULL text via ProseIndicatesWaiting and rewrites the same row to turn_done, and state_classifier's classifyAgentDone checks IsWaitingForUserInput BEFORE routing turn_done → ready, so the session goes working → waiting with NO ready in between — the scenario's defining criterion. The waiting is derived from the generic prose rule, so in the store this pause is indistinguishable from an ordinary trailing-question turn: hermes writes no structured approval marker (display_kind over the live store is only NULL/model_switch; its dangerous-command approval state lives module-level in memory in tools/approval.py and never becomes a message row). The cell therefore asserts the ARC, not a plan-specific signal. Recipe scope is entry into waiting only, per the scenario row's own note and the canonical claudecode sibling's spec; final state is waiting. Hermes carries a Process matcher, so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real `sessions` row is INSERTed only on the first user message — session_birth is anchored to start UNPINNED so the presession cannot steal identity, turn_start establishes the real session, and later phases chain via same_session_as. `model` is deliberately NOT pinned: the recording home's config.yaml is provisioned at record time, so record fills it from the recording.

text: The hermes session appears in ready. Unpinned: the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (the /plan expansion), not at launch, and a transient proc-<PID> presession may appear first.

The /plan turn drives the hermes session ready → working: message_count grows while the newest row is not assistant/finish_reason='stop'. The turn spans many 2s poll ticks (the model reads the ~6k-token skill body and writes the plan file), so the working leg is observed on its own merits.

The agent saves the plan and ends the turn asking for approval. The turn-boundary row (assistant/finish_reason='stop') carries the ask, so parser.go's PendingWaitingCue and turn_done land together and classifyAgentDone routes working → waiting — never through ready.
The waiting episode is user-visible and persists while the agent is gated on the plan decision — no skip-over to ready before any user reply. Final state is waiting.
